answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by licensing wandering seed couriers: each identity runs one fixed rural circuit, delivering yarrow seed packets to real farms, each handoff signed in person by the farmer and stamped onto a basalt waymarker at the gate. Random checks summon the courier to a waypoint within hours, and one courier cannot walk two circuits at once. The circuit fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real route, another set of farmers, another human walker, and twice the prior fee.
